extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Isabelle/Isar theorem-proving environment writing theory specifications, locales, classes, and proofs (proof engineers/formal-methods practitioners).
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and syntactic/semantic rules for writing Isabelle/Isar theory specifications: local theory targets, bundled declarations, term definitions, axiomatizations, locales, interpretations, and classes; includes command semantics, scoping, export behaviour, and recommended usage/constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local theory targets (context / begin / end)
rubrics_metrics.description: A local theory target is a specification context that is managed separately within the enclosing theory. Contexts may introduce parameters (fixed variables) and assumptions (hypotheses). Definitions and theorems depending on the context may be added incrementally later on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnamed contexts may introduce extra parameters/assumptions and results produced are generalized accordingly; named contexts refer to locales or type classes; local targets must be matched by end according to nesting rules; a global end concludes the theory itself (§5.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope modifiers: private and qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: private or qualified may be given as modifiers before any local theory command. This restricts name space accesses to the local scope, as determined by the enclosing context begin . . . end block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside its scope, a private name is inaccessible, and a qualified name is only accessible with some qualification. Neither a global theory nor a locale target provides a local scope by itself: an extra unnamed context is required to use private or qualified here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate target syntax (in c) for single commands
rubrics_metrics.description: (in c) given after any local theory command specifies an immediate target, e.g. “definition (in c)” or “theorem (in c)”. This works both in a local or global theory context; the current target context will be suspended for this command only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that “(in −)” will always produce a global result independently of the current target context. Any specification element that operates on local_theory implicitly allows the (in c) target syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export semantics of results from local contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and theorems produced within a local theory context are exported in a generic form suitable for the enclosing/global theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: a ≡ t[x] becomes c.a ?x ≡ t[?x] at the theory level together with a local abbreviation a ≡ c.a x. Theorems: a: B[x] becomes c.a: A[?x] =⇒ B[?x], discharging assumptions and generalizing parameters. Exact export depends on the underlying target infrastructure (locale, type class etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundled declarations: bundle / open_bundle / unbundle / print_bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: bundle b = decls defines a bundle of declarations in the current context. bundle b begin ... end defines a bundle from the body. open_bundle b activates and names the declarations immediately. unbundle b activates declarations from bundles in the current local theory context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bundles defined in local theory targets are subject to morphism transformations when moved into different application contexts. print_bundles prints named bundles available in the current context; the “!” option indicates extra verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundle activation variants: include / including / includes / opening
rubrics_metrics.description: include b activates the declarations from given bundles in a proof body (forward mode). including b is similar but works in proof refinement (backward mode). includes b applies to a confined specification context (unnamed contexts and long theorem statements). opening b is similar to includes but applies to named specification contexts (locales, classes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: include is analogous to note with expanded bundles; including is analogous to using; opening confines the effect to the surface context within the specification block and its begin/end block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundle polarity inversion via no prefix
rubrics_metrics.description: Bundle names may be prefixed by the reserved word no to indicate that the polarity of certain declaration commands should be inverted (e.g. syntax vs no_syntax, translations vs no_translations, notation vs no_notation, type_notation vs no_type_notation, adhoc_overloading vs no_adhoc_overloading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used recursively inside a bundle definition, no means that both the order and polarity of declarations is reversed (following algebraic group laws).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term definitions: definition and print_defn_rules
rubrics_metrics.description: definition c where eq produces an internal definition c ≡ t according to the specification given as eq, which is then turned into a proven fact. Deﬁnitions may be presented with explicit arguments on the LHS and additional conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The given proposition may deviate from internal meta-level equality according to the rewrite rules declared as defn by the object-logic. End-users normally need not change the defn setup. print_defn_rules prints definitional rewrite rules declared via defn in the current context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: abbreviation and print_abbrevs
rubrics_metrics.description: abbreviation c where eq introduces a syntactic constant associated with a certain term according to the meta-level equality eq. Abbreviations participate in type inference but are expanded before the logic sees them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretty printing of terms uses higher-order rewriting with rules from reverted abbreviations — take care to avoid overlapping or looping syntactic replacements. Optional mode restricts output to particular print mode; using “input” achieves one-way abbreviations. print_abbrevs prints constant abbreviations; “!” gives extra verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiomatization: use and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: axiomatization c1 . . . cm where ϕ1 . . . ϕn introduces several constants simultaneously and states axiomatic properties. The constants are marked as being specified once and for all, preventing additional specifications for the same constants later on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Axiomatization is restricted to a global theory context: local theory targets would introduce further uncertainty. Axiomatic specifications are required when declaring a new logical system within Isabelle/Pure; in application environments like Isabelle/HOL users normally prefer definitional mechanisms. Improper axiomatizations may disrupt well-formedness of a definitional theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic declarations: declaration / syntax_declaration / declare thms
rubrics_metrics.description: declaration d adds the declaration function d (ML type Morphism.declaration) to the current local theory under construction. syntax_declaration is similar but meant to affect only 'syntactic' tools by convention. declare thms declares theorems to the current local theory context (applying attributes) without theorem binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the (pervasive) option is given, the declaration is applied to all possible contexts involved, including the global background theory. Generic declaration elements are transformed according to morphisms for later application contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locale concept and hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: A locale is a functor mapping parameters (including implicit type parameters) and a specification to a list of declarations. Locale hierarchies are maintained as dependency graphs; dependencies can be introduced through import or by proving sublocale relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opening a locale appends to its list of declarations; during roundup redundant locale instances (subsumed ones) are omitted. The manual notes a separate document for a more detailed description of roundup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locale expressions and instance syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: A locale expression denotes a context composed of instances of existing locales. A locale instance consists of a reference to a locale and positional or named parameter instantiations, optionally followed by rewrites clauses. Identical instantiations may be omitted; “_” can omit an instantiation in positional form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terms in instantiations are from the surrounding context; the optional for clause defines local names or syntax. Instances may have an optional qualifier (mandatory or non-mandatory with “?”) that affects name spaces only. Rewrite clauses amend the morphism with equations acting as rewrite rules; they are available only in interpretation commands and must be proved by the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locale declaration elements: fixes, constrains, assumes, defines, notes
rubrics_metrics.description: In locale bodies, context elements include fixes x :: τ (mx) to declare parameters, constrains x :: τ to introduce type constraints (deprecated), assumes a: ϕ1 . . . ϕn to introduce local premises, defines a: x ≡ t to define previously declared parameters, and notes a = b1 . . . bn to reconsider facts within a local context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: defines is restricted to Pure equalities and the defined variable must be declared via fixes first. When defining derived operations, prefer definition (§5.4). (is p1 ... pn) patterns are illegal in locale definitions. notes may include attribute specifications (e.g., a local simp rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure of locale specifications: loc_axioms and loc predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: Locale specifications are 'closed up' by turning the given text into a predicate definition loc_axioms and deriving the original assumptions as local lemmas (modulo local definitions). The full cumulative view is provided on export via another predicate loc that refers to the complete specification text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicate arguments are those locale parameters that occur; these predicates operate at the meta-level in theory but the locale package attempts to internalize statements according to the object-logic setup. Separate introduction rules loc_axioms.intro and loc.intro are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous experiment locales (experiment ... begin)
rubrics_metrics.description: experiment body begin opens an anonymous locale context with private naming policy. Specifications in its body are inaccessible from outside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to perform experiments without polluting the global name space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locale inspection/visualization commands
rubrics_metrics.description: print_locale locale prints the contents of the named locale (omits notes by default; use print_locale! to include them). print_locales prints the names of all locales in the current theory; print_locales! gives extra verbosity. locale_deps visualizes all locales and their relations as a Hasse diagram (includes classes defined as locales).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ! option for extra verbosity where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locale interpretation: interpretation / interpret / global_interpretation / sublocale
rubrics_metrics.description: Locales may be instantiated and instantiated declarations added to the current context; this requires proof obligations and is called locale interpretation. interpretation interprets into a local theory (lifetime limited to the current context block), interpret interprets into a proof context (disappears at end of proof block), global_interpretation interprets into the global theory, and sublocale name ⊆ expr defines that name imports expr (requires a proof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation commands generate proof obligations; when discharged, instantiated declarations are post-processed and added. sublocale modifies the locale hierarchy dynamically; circular sublocale declarations are allowed if they do not lead to infinite chains. Rewrites clauses in expressions and defs (rewrite definitions) can be used to amend morphisms; rewrite equations must be proved by the user.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation-related proof support: intro_locales / unfold_locales / print_interps / trace_locales
rubrics_metrics.description: intro_locales and unfold_locales repeatedly expand introduction rules of locale predicates. print_interps lists all interpretations of a locale in the current theory or proof context. trace_locales, when true, prints locale instances activated during roundup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: intro_locales applies loc.intro only and helps understand which proof obligations originate from which locale instances; unfold_locales is more aggressive (applies loc_axioms.intro) and is part of the default method invoked behind the scenes. Use trace_locales when locale commands yield obscure errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caveats and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation may interact with other parts of the theory and tools in nontrivial ways (warnings provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notable warnings: if a global theory inherits declarations for a locale from one parent and an interpretation of that locale from another, the interpretation will not be applied to the declarations. Attributes are applied to interpreted theorems, so interpretation may modify the context of common proof tools (e.g. Simpliﬁer or Classical Reasoner) — manual declarations might be needed to revert such declarations. Interpretations may subsume previous interpretations if the latter are less general. interpretation (in c) ... is admissible but not useful since its result is discarded immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes: class / instantiation / instance / subclass semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: A class is a particular locale with exactly one type variable α. Beyond the underlying locale, a corresponding type class is established and is interpreted as an axiomatic type class whose logical content are the assumptions of the locale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: class c = superclasses bundles + body defines a new class inheriting from superclasses; fixes in body are lifted to the global theory level mapping the local type parameter α to ?α :: c; assumes are likewise lifted to global constants; c_class_axioms.intro is provided, but intro_classes method usually handles class membership proofs. instantiation t :: (s1,... ) s begin opens a target for specifying class operations at particular type instances; instance sets up a proof goal for the claimed type arities; subclass c in class context sets up proof that class c is contained in class d and interprets locale c into d on success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class tools: print_classes / class_deps / intro_classes
rubrics_metrics.description: print_classes prints all classes in the current theory. class_deps visualizes classes and their subclass relations as a directed acyclic graph with optional bounds. intro_classes repeatedly expands class introduction rules of the theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: intro_classes is usually part of the default proof step; trivial class instantiations may be performed by a single “..” proof step. class_deps can be restricted by upper/lower bounds to show only relevant parts of the graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rewrite definitions (defs) in interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Given definitions defs in an interpretation command produce corresponding definitions in the local theory’s underlying target and amend the morphism with rewrite rules stemming from the symmetric of those definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such rewrite definitions need not be proved explicitly by the user and are useful for interpreting concepts introduced through definitions. defs are processed sequentially without mutual recursion; defs are supported only where the target supports it.
